title: Ellsworth opioid treatment center opens with 200-patient capacity
also_topics: Jobs, housing, and cost of living
text:
An opioid treatment center recently opened in a leased space in Ellsworth to address the need for accessible substance use disorder treatment in the Downeast region. The center is located at 190 Bangor Road.
“People in Hancock County deserve access to high-quality opioid-use disorder treatment without having to travel long distances,” said Heather Camara, CEO of Everest Recovery Centers. “The opening of our clinic in Ellsworth helps ensure that residents in Downeast Maine can access life-saving treatment where they live, work and raise their families.”
The clinic provides outpatient treatment for opioid use disorder.
Five centers, four years
The limited liability corporation was started by a group of individuals who had worked together for many years in treating substance use disorder, Paul Makowski, the nonprofit’s COO, told Mainebiz.
“Founder David Piccoli put the team together to build Everest as a place that we would want to send a friend or family member and help individuals in need where there was a lack of available services,” Makowski said.
The Ellsworth location is Everest’s fifth center overall and its fourth in Maine, where it has locations in Saco, Manchester and South Portland. The home office team is remote and spread across Maine, Massachusetts and Rhode Island.
Private funding
Opening the Ellsworth location required adapting an existing building. The 5,500-square-foot layout includes six offices, a medical treatment room, dispensary, administrative office, group space, kitchen, lobby and common area.
The project was privately funded at an undisclosed cost.
The location has capacity for up to 200 patients, with room for growth. There are seven employees, and additional hiring is expected as programs grow. Across all of Everest’s locations, the organization serves about 800 people and employs around 70 people.
In the Downeast region, more than 8% of residents are estimated to be living with a substance use disorder, according to a news release. For many people in Hancock County and surrounding communities, accessing treatment has required traveling longer distances to larger population centers.
Bringing evidence-based medication-assisted treatment, counseling and recovery support services to Ellsworth allows patients to receive care closer to home, reducing barriers that often delay or prevent treatment.
“Everest is dedicated to helping people through their recovery journey and will be opening more clinics in the near future,” Makowski said.

title: Police: Suspect in child exploitation operation arrived to meeting with 2-year-old
text:
NEW ORLEANS (WVUE/Gray News) - A Louisiana police department said it made 10 arrests in an undercover Internet Crimes Against Children operation, which began Oct. 23.
The Kenner Police Department said the undercover operation targeted adults who used social media and online apps to solicit minors for sexual purposes.
This is the department’s fourth operation this year, officials said.
How the arrests were made
Detectives said they made 10 arrests during this latest operation. Six of those suspects engaged in explicit sexual conversations with people they believed were underage girls, police said. When the suspects arrived at the arranged meeting place, they were met by Kenner police and arrested.
Four others were arrested on warrants.
Suspect arrived with 2-year-old child
One suspect, Jasmine Gatlin, 40, of New Orleans, arranged to meet someone he believed was a 15-year-old girl, officials said. Undercover detectives told the suspect not to bring the 2-year-old with him, but he arrived with the child anyway, officials said.
Gatlin was arrested and the child was released into the care of the suspect’s grandmother, according to Kenner police. In addition to indecent behavior with a juvenile and computer-aided solicitation of a minor, Gatlin was charged with improper supervision of a minor by parent or legal custodian.
Those arrested
The 10 arrested in the operation were identified as:
- Douglas Glen Brown, 40, New Orleans
- Terrance Williams, 45, Des Allemands
- Dwayne Crisp, 43, New Orleans
- Troy Verrett Jr., 35, Marrero
- Jasmine Gatlin, 40, New Orleans
- Malcolm Richards, 39, New Orleans
- Kendrick Isom, 52, Vacherie
- Juan D. Gomez, 41, Kenner
- Tracey Rourke, 56, Gretna
- Paul Cordes III, 30, New Orleans
According to Kenner police, six suspects in the investigation are still at large.
- Thadis Misso II, 34, Union, Mississippi
- Dwayne Lewis, 43, Bridge City
- Leonardo Hernandez, 27, Weslaco, Texas
- Lloyd Allen, 32, Prairieville
- Baylee “Sabrina” Dawn Hogan, 27, Houston
- Russell Kyle Rouse, 37, Brunswick, Georgia
The 10 arrested individuals face indecent behavior with a juvenile and computer-aided solicitation of a minor charges. The six wanted individuals have outstanding warrants for those same offenses, officials said.
Police chief’s statement
“Every time we conduct one of these operations, we think we have seen it all. Bringing your own 2-year-old child to a meeting you believe is for sexual activity with a 15-year-old is beyond disturbing. Parents, we are trying our best to take these predators down, but we need your help. Please monitor your children on devices. They will thank you one day,” Kenner Police Chief Keith Conley said.

title: FBI says US has seized $1.2 billion worth of cryptocurrency stolen from Binance
text:
WASHINGTON (AP) — The FBI said Thursday that it had seized more than $1.2 billion of cryptocurrency reported stolen last month from Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange.
The theft of about $6.3 billion from Binance is regarded as the biggest crypto heist in history, and the FBI has previously attributed it to a North Korean hacking group known as TraderTraitor. The U.S. government and private sector have so far combined to freeze more than $2.7 billion of the stolen funds, and the Justice Department said Thursday that it has now obtained court authorization to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion of that total.
Typically in those situations, the U.S. government will file a claim of forfeiture with a judge, who will then determine who has a legitimate claim to the recovered funds.
Also Thursday, the FBI blamed North Korea for a separate social engineering scheme that officials say resulted in the theft of $400 million worth of cryptocurrency over the last 18 months. That scheme, known as FaceStealer, involves a complicated chain of events combining the hijacking of popular messaging apps and the recording of deepfake videos.
U.S. officials have repeatedly accused North Korea of using cyber schemes to generate funds for its regime, including its illicit weapons program.

title: Bond denied for man accused of burying his 11-month-old son alive
text:
LEXINGTON, S.C. (WIS/AP) – Bond was denied Thursday for the father accused of burying his 11-month-old son in a dog crate in a clump of scrubby pines.
Michael Comer showed no remorse for attempting to kill his son, Koah, and tried to leave the state, Tyler Douglas, lead investigator for the Lexington County Sheriff’s Department, told Judge Gary W. Reinhart. Reinhart approved a public defender for Comer and set a hearing for Dec. 10.
Comer, 25, is charged with attempted murder, unlawful conduct toward a child, custodial interference and burglary.
Comer has been in custody in Lexington County since Monday, when his son was reported missing.
An attorney for Comer has not yet been appointed.
Koah, who rescuers found after about 24 hours, was released from a hospital Tuesday night, Sheriff Jay Koon said.
Comer’s mother told authorities about previous suicidal statements her son had made and that he had talked about taking Koah to New York, where he claimed to have friends who could help him find work.
John Comer said he’d opened his home to his son and grandson on Monday after Michael Comer said they needed a place to stay. On Wednesday, he showed an Associated Press reporter the small hole on a neighbor’s property where rescuers uncovered the child.
“I cannot imagine how somebody could come to the point that that would be the right thing to do, or the thing to do at all,” John Comer told the AP.
Authorities haven’t revealed anything about Comer’s motive. He was sentenced in October to probation after pleading guilty to domestic violence involving the boy’s mother.
Koah’s parents “have had some situations,” the sheriff said.
“Children,” he said, “sometimes get caught in the middle.”
Dozens of first responders scoured the countryside for the boy with reddish blond hair. After a full day of searching, authorities found freshly disturbed soil and heard cries from below, the sheriff said.
“By the grace of God, [it] probably provided enough air for him to survive ur estimation of the last 24 hours under that dirt,” Koon said.
Koah was soon freed and “clinging to life,” the sheriff told reporters.

title: FIRST ALERT WEATHER: Sunshine Returns Thursday, With Weekend Storm Trending Farther South
text:
PRESQUE ISLE, Maine (WAGM) - Good evening everyone and happy Wednesday. I hope everyone had a great Veterans Day, and a big thank you to all those who have served our country. We had another day of mostly cloudy skies across the region today, with a few rain and snow showers once again making their way across portions of Aroostook County. Skies look to clear out some overnight tonight, allowing temperatures to fall back well below freezing for most locations. Sunshine makes a return to the region tomorrow, with a few more clouds expected heading into the afternoon hours. One of the bigger changes to our forecast today has been with the storm system we’ve been watching for this weekend, with the latest trends suggesting the majority of the precipitation will remain well to our south.
With cloud coverage decreasing heading into the overnight hours tonight, temperatures will have no problem cooling off into the upper teens and lower 20s for most locations. This will be a noticeably colder start to the day tomorrow compared to what we’ve seen the past couple of mornings. Winds are expected to remain fairly light overnight tonight, coming from a westerly direction around 5 mph. With the rain and snow showers we’ve seen over the past couple of days, I wouldn’t rule out a few slick spots on area roadways heading into tomorrow morning where any moisture remains on the pavement.
Tomorrow looks to be one of our nicer days weather-wise this week, with plenty of sunshine to start off the day. We’ll see some cloud coverage build back into the region heading into the afternoon hours, but I don’t expect it to ruin the day by any means. High temperatures tomorrow look to rebound into the upper 30s to lower 40s, which is right around where we should be for this time of year. Westerly winds remain light around 5 mph during the day tomorrow as well. If you have anything you need to get done outside, tomorrow would likely be the better of our next few days to do so.
As we head into the end of the work week, we’ll see more cloud coverage build into the region Friday. Over the past couple of days we’ve been discussing the potential for a coastal storm to develop and bring our region some accumulating snowfall heading into the upcoming weekend. The latest forecast guidance has continued to shift this system farther to our south, which has resulted in some changes to my thinking for this weekend. At this point, it looks like the immediate Downeast Coast has the best chance of seeing any precipitation directly associated with this coastal storm, with the majority of Northern Maine looking to miss out. That being said, I don’t think we’re completely out of the woods in terms of seeing snowflakes this weekend. An area of low pressure in the upper levels of the atmosphere will still be making its way over the region, allowing for some additional shower activity to develop. I think our best opportunity for seeing some snow showers will be Friday night into Saturday morning, before temperatures warm back above freezing Saturday afternoon, allowing for more rain showers to mix in. I’m not expecting much in the way of accumulating snowfall at this point, which is a bit of a change from what we were discussing earlier this week.
Mostly cloudy skies are likely to stick around for the second half of the weekend, with temperatures remaining in the upper 30s to around 40 degrees. Unfortunately, with the latest trends in our forecast, it also looks like we’ll be missing out on another opportunity for some beneficial precipitation across Northern Maine. For more details on what to expect the remainder of the work week, along with the latest information on our weekend forecast, make sure to check out my First Alert Video Forecast attached to this article. Have a great evening!

title: Suspect in deadly DC shooting was in legal battle with apartment management
text:
Suspect in deadly DC shooting was in legal battle with apartment management
A shooting at Vida Fitness in Washington, D.C., Thursday morning left four people injured and one dead and prompted a shelter-in-place order as police searched for the suspect.
A witness inside the gym said she heard a loud pop. She initially thought someone had dropped a weight but quickly realized it was a gunshot. She said she ran with others to a laundry room, where they barricaded themselves with 30 to 40 people until a SWAT team brought them to safety.
Another witness, Max Smith, said, "Eventually we hear three or four more shots. From there, we just started sprinting."
D.C. police confirmed that 46-year-old James Stewart, the building manager, was killed inside the gym. The suspect, identified as 55-year-old Matt Lambert, a medical doctor, barricaded himself inside his apartment near the scene. Lambert then shot four other people from his patio balcony, according to police.
"At this point in time, we don't know if there is a relationship between those other four victims and the suspect. We do know from the scene that those four suspects were shot by our suspect from his patio balcony area," Interim Chief Jeffery Carroll of the D.C. Metropolitan Police Department said.
Police said Lambert broke the gas line of his apartment's fireplace, started a fire and then shot himself. Lambert was confirmed dead.
Court records showed Lambert had been in an ongoing legal dispute with his apartment building's management over mold and moisture issues in his seventh-floor penthouse.

title: One man’s search for a hiking partner became a 5,000-member group honoring history
text:
RICHMOND, Va. (Aging Untold) — Dennis Bussey was looking for someone to go hiking with. Now he has thousands of people, and they also volunteer in the community.
How the group started
Bussey, who now lives in Lexington, Virginia, founded James River Hikers, which describes itself as “hiking with history.”
He had walked along the river by himself for a year and a half before starting the group.
“I thought, gosh, I wish I could find someone who would go hiking with me,” Bussey said.
After searching online, he found people to join him. The first meetup drew about seven people, and that was 14 years ago.
“Today we have 5,000 people,” Bussey said.
“We do hikes. We do history. We do social things. We do all kinds of things,” Bussey said.
Cleaning headstones
One of the hikers’ volunteer projects is cleaning gravestones at Shockoe Hill Cemetery.
The cemetery is the final resting place for some of Virginia’s historic figures:
- James Marshall, the nation’s fourth chief justice.
- Elizabeth Van Lew, a Civil War Union spy and abolitionist.
- Dr. William Foushee, the first mayor of Richmond.
When the group first started cleaning at the cemetery, headstones were not legible.
They started the work after they received permission from the city.
Bussey said Foushee was buried 201 years ago and that his headstone was “completely black.”
“Today is the 65th time we were out here cleaning these graves,” Bussey said. “We have cleaned probably 70% of all the stones in this cemetery.”
How the work is funded
Volunteers meet at the cemetery twice a month and scrub the stones.
The work is not cheap. Without donations and grants, the group would not be able to do it.
“Let’s go out and honor these folks and do this thing in a right way,” Bussey said. “And it’s a win-win for everybody.”

title: Man on trial for 2024 Bayside shooting claims self-defense
text:
PORTLAND — Trial has begun for a man accused of killing another man after a fight in the Bayside neighborhood two years ago.
Omar Abdelkader, 23, is accused of shooting and killing 31-year-old Edgar Cando on Oct. 28, 2024.
The defense did not dispute that during opening statements on Thursday in Cumberland County Superior Court, where Abdelkader pleaded not guilty in February to 2025 to a murder charge. His attorneys say he shot Cando in self-defense.
Both sides said they plan to show jurors a video of the shooting multiple times over the next several days.
According to opening statements and early testimony, the two men, who didn’t know each other, were on Portland Street near Dyer’s Variety Store that evening and had gotten into a fight. Cando landed one punch, knocking Abdelkader to the ground and injuring his nose, a prosecutor said. As Cando was walking away, with his back turned, Abdelkader fired his gun at him three times, a prosecutor said.
Defense attorney Amber Tucker said on Thursday that the video, recorded from 250 feet away, was only “part of the story,” and that Abdelkader plans to testify later in the trial. She said Abdelkader was afraid, that he suffers a seizure disorder and believed Cando had “slashed” him with a knife.
“And in those seconds, Omar believed that Edgar Cando was about to kill him or seriously hurt him,” Tucker said.
Abdelkader is a U.S. citizen who has lived in Portland since he was 10, Tucker said, moving here from Egypt to live with his father. His other attorney, Tina Nadeau, said earlier this week that his name was originally misspelled by Portland police and in court records as “Abd Elkader.”
Assistant Attorney General Kate Bozeman told the jury she is confident that the state’s evidence will support a guilty verdict.
Bozeman said that both men fought in an area “where people congregate and fights sometimes break out.” She argued that Abdelkader shot Cando because he had been “bested in a fistfight.”
She said Abdelkader left the scene with his girlfriend at the time. She was charged in 2025 with one count of hindering apprehension and her case is still pending, according to court records.
Abdelkader turned himself into the police station about three hours later, Bozeman said, bringing with him the firearm that was used in the shooting.
She showed the jury a picture of Cando, taken before Oct. 28, where he’s standing in front of a beach and smiling. A few of Cando’s family members were in court on Thursday, and his partner at the time of the shooting, Quantia Moran, was the first witness called to testify.
She told the jury they shared a son, and that she was standing beside Cando, their backs to Abdelkader, when he started shooting.
“He was a father. He was someone’s son, a brother — a human being that should still be here today,” Bozeman said. “His life, his future, was stolen.”

title: Black Friday scams to watch for and how to avoid them
also_topics: Jobs, housing, and cost of living
text:
(InvestigateTV) — Some Black Friday deals can cost shoppers more than they save, and Kyle James, a writer for ConsumerAffairs, identified the biggest red flags this year.
The first is what are known as “ghost websites.” These are fake sites promoted through phony social media ads with offers that seem too good to be true.
“The ads are really convincing. Sometimes they’ll use celebrities in their ads. They’ll use some really good marketing tools. You’ll see brands that you recognize. And a lot of people will click on it and go to these ghost websites, and those websites are designed to either place your order, and you never see the product. Or they’re going to steal your credit card information and you’re never going to hear from them again,” James said.
Before clicking, shoppers can type the company’s name into a browser and search it with the word “scam.”
Another trick involves social media ads claiming a “store closing” or “final close-out.” The ads send shoppers to a fake website that collects their personal information.
Another scam involves fake customer service numbers.
“A lot of times these scammers will buy sponsored Google listings for like ‘BestBuy’ customer service, and in many cases, it will be up above the actual BestBuy phone number. And they want you to call it and they’re going to get you and try to get your credit card information or try to do something nefarious,” James said.
Shoppers should use a store’s app or official website to find the real customer service number.
The final scam involves text messages about a “delayed delivery” or a “problem with your order.”
James said a legitimate company will not text customers to verify a tracking number or an address. Shoppers should not click links in those texts or give any information.

title: Family of Bangor soldier killed at Pearl Harbor prepares to say goodbye
text:
BANGOR, Maine (WABI) - Nearly 85 years after a Bangor soldier was killed in the attack on Pearl Harbor, his family is preparing to say goodbye.
Pfc. Willard Carleton Orr was 21 when he was killed at Hickam Field in Hawaii. His remains were identified last year and recently returned to Maine.

title: Nvidia stock falls following CEO resignation
text:
Nvidia stock falls following CEO resignation
Nvidia stock falls following CEO resignation
Nvidia stocks fell sharply Thursday morning following news that founder and CEO Jensen Huang resigned following reports he was the target of a "foreign intelligence effort."
The stock dropped 12.6% at opening Thursday, to $150.99.
The New York Times first reported Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy last month. On Sunday, Nvidia's board announced an investigation, and Huang issued a statement to employees posted on their website, admitting to the affair.
The AI chip supplier is the second highest valued company in the world, behind Apple and ahead of Microsoft, Google and Amazon. Its total market capitalization is estimated to be more than $4 trillion.
Founded in 1993, Nvidia started selling stocks to the public in 1999 at a value of four cents a share. The company's focus was graphics processing units, or GPUs, for video gaming.
The value of the company didn't take off until the launch of ChatGPT in 2022. At that time, the value of a share was about $17. Now, the bulk of its revenue is made from data centers.
Nvidia stock already took a tumble last week, dropping 10% last Thursday. It was the worst day for major stock indexes since April 2025, according to Yahoo Finance. The declines impacted Nvidia along with other AI chipmakers. On Monday, Nvidia stock dropped following weekend reports about the company's investigation into the CEO's affair.

title: Regional snow show brings touch of winter to Portland
also_topics: Jobs, housing, and cost of living
text:
Representatives from Maine’s ski areas, outdoor businesses and more than 2,500 winter sports enthusiasts gathered in Portland last weekend to kick off the upcoming season.
Organized by Maine Outdoor Brands and Thompson’s Point, the inaugural First Tracks: Northeast Snow Show featured more than 60 vendors, presentations by winter sports experts, gear demonstrations and outdoor films. The event took place on Saturday and Sunday.
“We couldn’t be more thrilled with First Tracks’ first year, from the turnout to the vendor experience to the caliber of speakers,” said Jenny Kordick, executive director of Maine Outdoor Brands.
“Extra touches made it feel like a true celebration of winter: films on the big screen, free gear repairs and a Kids’ Zone that kept the whole family engaged,” she added. “Our outdoor community is strongest when we collaborate, and this weekend proved it.”
Kordick was a Mainebiz 40 Under 40 honoree in 2023.
Program highlights included presentations by meteorologist Keith Carson and ski celebrity Donny Pelletier, who discussed the upcoming winter season. Maine ski industry professionals also gave talks about snowmaking mountain operations.
The event took place on the eve of ski season in Maine, with Sugarloaf Mountain set to open Nov. 20 and Pleasant Mountain aiming to open the weekend of Dec. 5, according to their websites.
First Tracks organizers are planning a second edition in 2027.

title: Fire in White Mountain National Forest now nearly 60% contained
text:
Wild River Fire in White Mountain National Forest now nearly 60% contained
Firefighters continue to secure and strengthen containment of the Wild River Fire, a wildfire that has been burning in the White Mountain National Forest for nearly two weeks.
The U.S. Forest Service said that the fire was 59% contained as of Wednesday and was burning 817 acres. Those figures had not changed as of Thursday morning's update.
Officials said Thursday that crews are reinforcing existing fire lines and using natural barriers to contain the fire within its existing perimeter, and that they remain focused on suppressing hot spots, as well as monitoring, patrol and mop-up operations.
According to the Forest Service, fire behavior remains minimal with heat limited to isolated pockets in duff. Ongoing infrared flights conducted by unmanned aircraft systems continue to identify and assess potential hot spots within the fire area, supporting suppression and monitoring efforts.
As of Thursday morning, a total of 58 personnel were working to suppress the fire, including one helicopter, one unmanned aerial system and one suppression module.
The image below shows a map of the Wild River Fire as of Wednesday, Nov. 11.
The Wild River Fire was first reported the afternoon of Nov. 1, just southeast of Gorham, New Hampshire, and just south of Gilead, Maine, near Evans Notch.
On Nov. 4, the Forest Service issued a closure order that remains in effect. Click here to see a map of the closure.
On Nov. 5, officials revealed that they believed the fire was caused by humans. Two community meetings have been held since then in order to share information with people who live in the area and to answer questions from residents.
The Forest Service announced Tuesday that the Wild River Fire was more than half contained.
Fire personnel are also identifying and addressing suppression repair needs for roads, trails and other infrastructure that have been impacted during the firefighting efforts.
The Forest Service said fire severity has generally been low across the fire area, and that the fire has primarily been consuming leaf litter with limited impacts to larger vegetation such as trees and shrubs.
Due to the minimal fire activity and a favorable outlook, officials said the incident has transitioned from a Type 3 to a Type 4 fire.

title: Democrats flock to Denver for a post-midterms introspection-turned-celebration
text:
Democrats flock to Denver for a post-midterms introspection-turned-celebration
Fresh off the best electoral performance in half a century, Democratic officials and strategists converged on Denver Thursday to plot a further course for the party and revel in their gains.
The two-day What's Next conference, hosted by a new group called Majority Democrats, was put on politicos' calendars months ago as another stepping stone as the party charted its way out of its post-2024 political wilderness.
Now Democrats will have to figure out what to do with majorities in both chambers of Congress and control of at least 12 new state legislative chambers.
"America tried on hate, and it didn't fit," Denver Mayor Mike Johnston said as he kicked off the event.
The schedule includes some of the victorious candidates from the midterms, such as Texas Sen.-elect James Talarico and Iowa Sen.-elect Josh Turek.
Also, there will be potential presidential hopefuls, such as former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg, New Jersey Sen. Cory Booker and Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro.
It's a who's-who of rising Democratic talent that will also make the event a showcase for the party.
The gathering is also a showcase of sorts for Denver, which remains in the hunt for the party's 2028 convention after last hosting one in 2008. The city is selling itself as a modern example of a purple state turning solid blue.
The group Majority Democrats seeks to bridge the traditional left-center splits that have riven the party for years, particularly since the 2024 election that returned President Donald Trump to the White House. It particularly positions itself as the voice of a new generation of party leaders tired of old ideological and establishment battles, and the speaker list skews noticeably young.
The conference also includes various party leaders, such as the likely next House speaker, Hakeem Jeffries, who has engendered suspicion among some on the left who continue to target the party's Washington power structure.

title: Rockland to require owners to register vacant commercial buildings
also_topics: Jobs, housing, and cost of living
text:
Rockland’s City Council gave final approval Monday night Nov. 9 to a local law to require the owners of vacant commercial and multi-unit apartment buildings to register their properties.
The law takes effect Dec. 9. Within 90 days from then, the owners of all existing vacant commercial, industrial and residential buildings with three or more units must apply for a vacant commercial property certificate.
The cost for the certificate is $500 per year.
Owners would need to provide information including the cellphone number of someone to reach 24 hours a day if there is a problem with the property.
Any owner who fails to apply for or obtain a certificate in accordance with the requirements of this ordinance will be deemed in violation and subject to a fine of up to $1,000 per property for the first violation and up to $2,000 for every subsequent violation.
The vote was 4-1 with Councilor Nicole Kalloch voting against the ordinance.
Buildings undergoing renovations would be exempt.
Richard Rockwell, who owns several downtown properties, said his properties would not be affected by the new law but warned that there could be unintended consequences. He voiced concern that buildings that had retail on the lower level but empty upper floors could be impacted by the law. He said the definition of the ordinance, if a property was more than 50% vacant it would be considered a vacant building.
“No one wants an empty building. Businesses don’t want empty buildings. I don’t want empty buildings. It’s not good for the community,” Rockwell said. But, he said, it could send the wrong message to property owners.
Rockwell’s Rockland Realty stated that the city should look at why there are so many empty buildings and what role the city plays in that.
Former Councilor Joseph Steinberger said he hoped the city’s code office would work with owners of these vacant buildings and see what can be done to help them make the properties productive.
Councilor Penny York, who along with Councilor Kaitlin Callahan, developed the ordinance, said the goal of the ordinance was for the city to work with owners and direct them to resources that could help develop the vacant properties. York noted that the fee imposed by Rockland is much less than other communities who have similar laws.
The purpose of the ordinance is to “protect the health, safety, and general welfare of the people of the City of Rockland by establishing a program to identify and certify vacant commercial, industrial, and residential buildings in the City, and determine the actions property owners will take to return those vacant buildings to productive use or occupancy. This ordinance is intended to prevent or mitigate dangers to health, safety, and welfare, promote responsible management, provide safe neighborhoods for residents and visitors, safeguard property values, prevent affiliated municipal costs from being passed on to taxpayers, expedite building repairs, and provide for prompt contact with property owners by police, fire, and code enforcement when issues or emergencies develop and for enforcement of these provisions.”
Resident Kyle Swan praised Rockwell for developing properties, but noted there were still vacant buildings on Main Street with plywood on the building.
Two of the most visible long vacant commercial buildings are on Route 1. The old Burger King at 49 Camden St. has been closed since December 2020. The property is owned by Ruth Salemme of Houston, Texas. The property has been for sale but no buyers have come forward.
The asking price is $800,000. The city has the property assessed at $880,000. The property has eight-tenths of an acre with a 1977-built building of 3,100 square feet.
The former Irving convenience store/gas station at 3 Camden St. has been closed since 2015. Renovations are in progress at the former Irving building but there are no plans for the space, according to the city planner. The Irving property is owned by Spirit SPE Portfolio 2012-2 LLC, a limited liability company based in San Diego, California. Irving Oil Retail Sales LLC has a lease on the property through May 1, 2028, with an option to renew eight times for five years each.
A dilapidated house at 2 Pine St., at the intersection of Warren Street, will be torn down soon, City Manager Tom Luttrell said. The project has taken longer for asbestos removal, the manager said. The Council approved Nov. 9, approving an additional $30,000 for the removal of the house. The city will place a lien on the property equal to the city’s costs. When the property is sold, the city will recover its money.
Councilor York noted that she has been having discussions with the mayor on efforts to use the downtown space on Oak Street for activities that could enliven the downtown.
Luttrell updated the Council at the Nov. 9 meeting on revenues received from parking meters. He said that coordinating the software company and meter company prevented the city from expanding metered parking as had been approved by the Council earlier in the year. He said it would be in place for next year.
The City took in $72,573 in parking meter revenues in 2026, which was down about $8,000 from 2025. He said that this coincided with a decline in retail sales in 2026.
The Council voted unanimously April 15 to expand metered parking to Elm Street, Museum Street, Custom House Place, and Main Street (from Park Street to Summer Street). In the past two years, metered parking was limited to city-owned parking lots on Winter Street, behind the Thorndike complex, the Custom House lot, and 22 spaces along Tillson Avenue. Those lots will remain paid parking.
The changes were made to generate additional dollars to offset the need for additional property taxes. Parking costs $2 an hour for the spaces designated as paid parking spaces. Rockland residents, however, get two hours of free parking per day. City residents can pick up decals for free at the city clerk’s office to get the two hours per day of free parking. Those decals need to be displayed while parking in metered locations.

title: Electric vehicle owners could soon face annual federal fee under proposed bill
also_topics: Jobs, housing, and cost of living
text:
(CNN) - Owning an electric vehicle may soon cost more.
A surface transportation bill moving through Congress would require electric vehicle owners to pay an annual federal fee beginning at $130.
The fee could then increase by $5 each year, with a maximum of $150, according to the proposed legislation.
Owners of plug-in hybrids would have to pay $35.
Current funding for surface transportation is set to expire next month. The electric vehicle fees could take effect as soon as December if approved by Congress.
The government uses money it collects from gasoline taxes to help pay for road projects. Electric vehicles do not require gasoline, so those drivers do not pay that tax.
Supporters of the measure said it ensures electric vehicle drivers help pay for the roads they use.

title: Two roads diverge in front of Chuck Schumer
text:
Sen. Chuck Schumer has a choice to make about his legacy.
Schumer can continue to aspire to be majority leader of the Senate again, and become one of the reasons the Democratic Party fails in two years. He has been ineffective during the entirety of the Trump years. There is no reason to expect anything different from him.
Or he can make himself into a true hero by putting the United States, the American people (who spoke so loudly last week) and the Constitution ahead of his ego. If he removes himself from the running, he will be remembered as someone who listened to the voters and understands that righting our ship of state, which is currently foundering, is more important than any one person.
We need a warrior to champion the Constitution, first and foremost. Schumer is a decent man, with much knowledge to share and good intentions, but he is not the general we need right now. Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse (RI), Sen. Tammy Duckworth (IL), Sen. Mark Kelly (AZ), Sen. Cory Booker (NJ) and others who have been vocal and assertive throughout the the last two years are better prepared for the future; they recognize the reality of the present.
Sen. Schumer developed his political skills in the last century; they worked then. We are now fighting a regime that does not box — it is manned by street fighters with no consideration of rules or laws.
Jenifer Duryea
Limington

title: Patriots hope trip to Germany is fresh start
text:
MUNICH — New England Patriots tight end Hunter Henry is still trying to block out memories of a 10-6 loss to the Indianapolis Colts in Frankfurt, Germany, three years ago.
DeMario Douglas said he got food poisoning the following season when the Patriots lost to Jacksonville in London.
New England gets another chance on the international stage Sunday against the Detroit Lions in Munich. The Patriots are coming off a blowout loss to the Packers and hope to avoid falling to .500 heading into their bye week.
“It’s the NFL, it’s a high-pressure business, it’s a high-pressure sport,” quarterback Drake Maye said Thursday after a short practice at Bayern Munich’s facilities. “So, I think there’s pressure to play well every Sunday and to come out with a win.”
In his rookie season in 2024, Maye made his second NFL start and was a lone bright spot in a 32-16 loss to the Jaguars at Wembley Stadium. He threw for 276 yards and two touchdowns.
Then-coach Jerod Mayo labeled the team “soft” after its sixth straight loss.
The year prior, Patriots fans suffered through the loss to Indianapolis in Frankfurt. Mac Jones was benched.
This is where we come to a Tom Brady reminder. The Patriots won three international games with Brady at the helm: 2009 and 2012 at Wembley and in 2017 in Mexico City.
A.J. Brown and Rhamondre Stevenson at practice
The Patriots (5-4) arrived in Bavaria on Thursday morning and held a light jog-through practice amid some late-afternoon sprinkles.
The big questions entering the weekend will be the availability of receiver A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) and running back Rhamondre Stevenson (knee). Brown was limited in practice Wednesday and participated Thursday, when players did some straight-line jogging during the portion open to reporters.
“It feels good, just to have that leader back,” Douglas said of Brown. “Every time he’s on the field, I learn.”
Brown, the team’s top offseason acquisition, has just nine receptions for 101 yards so far this season.
Stevenson worked out on the side Thursday as his teammates stretched and jogged. The team’s leading rusher (399 yards on 102 carries) hurt his knee last week against the Packers.
Maye said Stevenson at practice “speaks to first off the media not really knowing 100% what they’re talking about a lot of the time, and … a guy that wants to be out there.”
Before traveling Wednesday night, the Patriots ruled out LG Ben Brown (knee), CB Carlton Davis III (knee) and RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness). They are still without without Week 1 starting right guard Mike Onwenu (ankle) and left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring), who are both currently on injured reserve.
Paris next?
The NFL has shown no signs of slowing its international push. This season there are a record nine international games. Last month, Paris hosted for the first time.
“That would be cool to play in Paris,” Maye said when asked where else he’d like to play.
The quarterback recalled his grandmother speaking fluent French when he was growing up.
“Me and my brothers, we speak a little bit, not great,” he said of his French skills.
Henry was asked a similar question.
“Where do I want to play next? Gillette Stadium,” he said to chuckles from the assembled reporters, before adding “maybe like the Bahamas or the Caribbean.”
Maye says Kane should chase NFL kicking dream
Maye fully endorses Harry Kane’s dream of one day becoming an NFL kicker.
Maye spoke Thursday after practice at the campus of Bayern Munich — Kane’s soccer team.
“It would be cool to see him try,” Maye said. “He’s dealt with pressure, that’s one of the biggest things about kicking in the National Football League is the pressure of it. He does that for a living. So, I don’t think he’d have any problem.”
Kane, a longtime Patriots fan, recently became the first Englishman in 25 years to win the Ballon d’Or, soccer’s award for the best player in the world.
The 33-year-old England captain this month signed a contract extension to stay at Bayern until 2029, so it’s unclear when he’d be ready to give NFL kicking a shot.
Kane has mused over the years about trying it. He even has floated the idea of combining his NFL dream with joining a Major League Soccer team.
“I think I’ve seen him maybe kick a few and he looked pretty good,” Maye said. “No doubt, he does that for a living, so I’m sure he’d be just fine.”

title: Witnesses who watched a Brooklyn building come crashing down felt helpless amid the chaos
text:
NEW YORK (AP) — Before the screams started, Dervie Mapp heard loud popping noises outside her Brooklyn apartment. She bolted out of bed to the kitchen window and watched as a neighboring building came crashing down, raining three stories of bricks and twisted metal.
Stunned survivors cried out amid thick dust and piles of rubble that moments earlier had been people’s homes.
“I saw the whole thing come down,” Mapp, a 67-year-old retiree, told The Associated Press on Thursday. “People were running up out of the pit, screaming and hollering. I couldn’t believe it — I froze.”
The deadly collapse that occurred without warning Wednesday afternoon took down a building that housed a store selling medical uniforms on the ground level and four apartments on the floors above.
At least eight people perished, including two children. Officials said 18 others suffered injuries.
New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani on Thursday described the victims as “parents and children, young families building their lives in our city and immigrants from Mexico, Colombia, Ecuador, Trinidad and beyond.”
Among those hurt were four firefighters assisting with rescue efforts, which continued Thursday as crews searched for survivors through heaps of debris that included mattresses, a broken sink and a refrigerator with its door missing and food jumbled inside. Vinyl records, shoes and other personal belongings littered the rubble.
James Williams said he heard loud banging at the construction site all day Wednesday as he worked at a deli across the street. He said he noticed bricks falling from a building next to the site. Then the whole building fell down.
The collapse ripped away a wall shared with an adjacent building, which remained standing with the interiors of its apartments exposed — closets crammed with clothing, a stuffed bear sitting atop a pile of shoes and laundry heaped on a pink bedspread.
Security camera video from the building showed an interior stairway shaking as the wall beside it fell in a loud crash and a cloud of dust. The camera later recorded a firefighter helping a resident descend the same stairs above a yawning abyss of debris.
“Nice and easy,” the firefighter said as the person clutched both his hand and the railing.
Despite the chaos, construction workers who had barely escaped with their lives turned around and began clawing through the wreckage to free survivors, said Mamdani. He said their swift actions saved lives.
The mayor said Thursday that two construction workers were among the dead.
They included 26-year-old José Luis Caguana Cosquillo, an immigrant from Ecuador who had a young child and pregnant wife. His brother, Carlos Caguana, told WNBC-TV that he was one of the people killed.
“He was the sole provider for the family,” Caguana said, adding that his brother’s wife was devastated.
“She’s completely overwhelmed,” he said, “and can’t even find the words to speak.”
___
Rico reported from Atlanta. AP journalists Russ Bynum in Savannah, Georgia; Hannah Fingerhut in Des Moines, Iowa; and Scott Bauer in Madison, Wisconsin, contributed.

title: Man accused of running over and killing mother after argument about borrowed car, police say
text:
TULSA, OKLA. (Gray News) - An Oklahoma man is accused of running over and killing his mother after an argument about a borrowed car, according to authorities.
John Tiffin, 31, was arrested on charges of second-degree murder, assault and battery with a dangerous weapon, reckless driving and obstructing an officer, a press release said.
Tiffin allegedly borrowed his mother’s silver car on Oct. 7 to run errands but never returned it. His mother was identified as 69-year-old Karen Curthoys.
Police said Curthoys wanted her car back and contacted her other son, Timothy Curthoys, who agreed to help her recover the vehicle.
Tulsa police said Curthoys and her son tracked down the car.
According to court documents, they found the car in a driveway. An argument followed as Timothy attempted to recover it.
Tiffin allegedly put the car in reverse and hit his mother, who was standing outside between two vehicles. Timothy was in the front passenger seat.
Karen Curthoys was taken to a hospital, where she died from her injuries on Oct. 12.

title: This country band is breaking the mental health stigma among veterans
text:
NEW ORLEANS (InvestigateTV) - A group of veterans has turned their shared experiences into a mission, using country music to address mental health stigma in the military community.
Vet Jams, a band that performs at bars around the New Orleans metro area, combines live music with open conversations about therapy and mental health support for veterans.
“I literally get on the microphone and say it’s okay to go to therapy. And people will turn around from the bar. It’s weird. Right? And it’s not a normal thing. But that’s kind of the idea,” said Jason Davey, the band’s leader and a Marine veteran who served in Iraq in 2003.
Personal tragedy sparked military service
Davey said his decision to enlist began with family tragedy.
“My brother actually signed up before me. He was a few years older, and unfortunately, he passed away. So, we had the full 21-gun salute. And after his funeral, I just kind of got it in my head that I wanted to finish his enlistment. So, I signed up so I could finish what he started,” Davey said.
After serving overseas, Davey married, started a family and settled in New Orleans. Years later, he faced another loss.
“I lost my wife about four years ago now, and I started my therapy journey before she passed away. And it just kind of made me realize how important it is. And there’s just a lot of people in the military that don’t seek that avenue. It’s this kind of social stigma that really exists in the military,” Davey said.
Veterans find connection through shared experience
Davey said therapy helped save him, along with connections with other veterans who understood his experiences.
“I’ve never told my wife anything about being in Iraq, but you will tell a complete stranger sitting at the bar stool next to you everything about it. There’s just certain rapport and trust that you have with somebody else that’s been through the same thing,” Davey said.
Three years ago, Davey partnered with Army veteran Chet Pierson to form Vet Jams.
“Me and Jason Davey, we were sitting right here, talking about mental health. He’s like, I play guitar. I play harmonica. He’s like, I got a great idea. Let’s form a band and start talking about mental health for veterans,” Pierson said.
Mission targets veteran suicide rates
Pierson, who served in Desert Storm and was diagnosed with post-traumatic stress disorder in 1992, said the band’s mission is to meet veterans where they are.
“The 22 a day, 6000 a year for 20 years. And more veterans kill themselves than we have in combat. You know, that’s a staggering number,” Pierson said.
More than 20 musicians have played with Vet Jams in a rotating lineup of veterans using music as support.
“Togetherness can save lives. Music saves lives. Camaraderie saves lives,” Pierson said.
The band performs for free and hopes to take the stage at Jazz Fest one day. More information is available at vetjams.org.

title: 5 people are shot in a trendy DC neighborhood, including 1 killed at a gym, then suspect kills self
text:
WASHINGTON (AP) — A man in a long-running dispute over the conditions of his penthouse condo shot and killed the building manager in a busy gym Thursday before fleeing and shooting four more people from his patio in just minutes, shocking a popular capital neighborhood and attracting a swarm of police officers.
Matt Lambert, a 55-year-old doctor, then fatally shot himself while holed up in his apartment, where he had been speaking by phone with police negotiators, said Jeffery Carroll, interim chief with the Metropolitan Police Department.
Lambert was locked in rancorous litigation with management over mold and moisture problems in his seventh-floor unit, court records show.
Mayor Muriel Bowser said she was “devastated” at the loss of life in a “senseless act of gun violence.”
The shootings occurred around 8 a.m. in Logan Circle, about a mile (1.6 kilometers) north of the White House. Much of the block on 15th Street Northwest was cordoned off as police urged people to avoid the area, which includes a VIDA Fitness center, St. Luke’s Episcopal Church, residences and a Whole Foods store. Schools were locked down.
Chaos in less than 5 minutes
Law enforcement SWAT teams and other officers had their guns drawn on the roof of a building and on the ground below. Carroll said Lambert, armed with three guns, shot and wounded four people from his condo patio. Three sustained non-life-threatening injuries and the fourth remained in critical condition by late afternoon.
“This whole incident took place in less than five minutes. ... I can only imagine being in that area and hearing the gunshots or being inside the gym,” he said.
The man killed at VIDA gym on the ground floor was identified as James Stuart, 46, the building manager, the police chief said.
“There has been an ongoing dispute between the suspect in this case” and management “regarding maintenance issues, mold and the like. We believe it’s related to that,” Carroll said.
Lambert had filed a lawsuit, alleging that he hadn’t been able to enjoy his penthouse since 2024 because of mold, moisture and water problems, records show. He claimed the problems began after a contractor had worked on the building’s exterior.
The litigation was ongoing, according to court filings. Lambert appeared to share his condo woes, including photos and an engineering report, on an X site titled OfMiceandMold. The report was described online as “my manifesto.”
Speaking to reporters, Lambert’s lawyer, Joel Braithwaite, said he was “deeply shaken and saddened” by the violence. He said the condo resembled a “war zone” because of its conditions and said Lambert had spent more than $300,000 in pressing the lawsuit.
“I don’t think there’s any sense to be made,” Braithwaite said of the shootings. “I can’t give you that closure.”
Braithwaite said Lambert had lived in the unit since 2017. Online property records show he bought it in September 2016 for nearly $1.1 million.
Gym members scrambled when they heard shots
James Spellman, who was at the gym, said there were about 50 people there when the shootings began.
“Within seconds there was a man who fell to the ground, and a pool of blood came out,” he said. “One gym member rushed to help him. He was instantly dead. He had been shot in the neck.”
Anthony Mirones was in the gym’s cardio area when he heard a loud bang and thought something fell off the wall. He said someone was trying to help the wounded man but then a fire alarm went off and many people ran.
“The people in cardio had to step over the body,” Mirones said.
Another witness, Ryan Dubicki, said he was in his nearby apartment around the same time when he “heard about five bangs.”
“They were really spread out so I thought it was construction,” said Dubicki, an AP employee on the elections team. A short time later “there were cops everywhere.”
While inside his condo, Lambert also cut a natural gas line to the fireplace and started a fire, triggering the sprinkler system, which quickly contained the flames, Carroll said.
The Washington Sun posted an online story by Michael Brice-Saddler, who said he had interviewed Lambert last year about his condo problems. Lambert had told another resident that he knew Stuart’s morning routine at the VIDA gym.
“If you want to see the building manager,” Brice-Saddler quoted Lambert as saying, “he comes in the gym about 8 o’clock.”
___
This story has been corrected to show the interim police chief’s name is Jeffery, not Jeffrey.
___
Associated Press writers Ed White in Detroit, Rebecca Santana and Gary Fields in Washington, Dave Collins in Hartford, Conn., and Christopher Weber in Los Angeles contributed to this report.

title: Bar Harbor Historical Society lays off entire staff
main_topic: Jobs, housing, and cost of living
text:
The Bar Harbor Historical Society has laid off all five of its paid staff.
“All the staff fears for that collection,” former Executive Director Erin Cough said. “We’ve been told there will be no new exhibits next year … there will be no programming next year.”
Cough said the layoffs came after she had previously been assured by board members that there were no plans to let people go. She said staff were shocked when they were told the news, leaving them with few options right before the holiday season, when hiring typically slows.
The historical society has been operating in a deficit over the past four years, according to its IRS filings.
In 2024, expenses outpaced revenues by more than $128,000.
Since the historical society bought La Rochelle, a 123-year-old Gilded Age chateau, its contribution and grants income has waned year after year while its expenses have crept up.
But Cough said the nonprofit’s finances improved last year with revenue of more than $700,000, and staff could have closed the gap with more time.
It’s not clear how the layoffs will affect the organization’s operation of La Rochelle, but board members plan to monitor the museum while it’s closed to the public for the season.
In an email to staff, board members said they will take the winter for “thoughtful organizational restructuring.”
